newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - May 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - May 12.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Monday:
* An earthquake hit northeastern Iran, killing at least 2,400 people.

* The initial unity among state attorneys general in lawsuits against the tobacco industry may be eroding over the issue of liability for smoking-related claims, people familiar with negotiations said.
* The popularity of mini-vans, once the vehicle of choice for suburban families, is waning and sales have been dropping after more than a decade of being on the rise.
* World chess champion Garry Kasparov resigned the sixth and final game against Deep Blue, the I.B.M. computer.
* In contrast to its emotional opponent, Deep Blue remains seemingly unmoved and silent in its victory over the human chess champion, Garry Kasparov.
* The families of the 400 black men infected with syphilis who were left untreated in the Tuskegee experiment begin to emerge from their years of suffering in silence.

* New York Gov. George Pataki proposed lifting rent-control protections for a small group of wealthy tenants immediately in a compromise designed to find middle ground between Republicans and Democrats.
* The New York Rangers national hockey team and the New York Knicks basketball team each win games in their respective playoff games.
